harvest_trust.cnmr: Most useful harvest channel, especially for relative ordering and separated resonances, but not uniformly accurate to ±3 ppm. Nitrobenzene supports conventional substituent increments. Several aliphatic methyl positions appear about 4–5 ppm high, and acetone 195.1 is inconsistent with its usual carbonyl near 207 ppm. Benzaldehyde and toluene each require five chemically distinct carbon environments despite four harvested sticks. Use chemistry-scale priors, flag suspect positions, and do not fit a global offset from this pack. Intensities are not carbon counts.
harvest_trust.hnmr: Use as provisional envelope positions, not complete chemical-environment counts or multiplicities. Nitrobenzene and the alcohol/ester regions provide useful checks. Benzaldehyde 8.38/6.66/6.38 and acetic-acid methyl 3.46 are inconsistent with normal assignments by more than the stated tolerance. Acetone methyl 2.53 is also somewhat high. n_lines is not multiplicity, and I is not an integral. Exchangeable-proton shifts are solvent-, concentration-, and temperature-dependent.
harvest_trust.ir: Do not retune IR in this task. Ignore flat_fail rows for IR calibration; their NMR data remain independently assessable. Even ok rows contain false minima. Ethanol OH near 3230 cm^-1 and C-O near 1050 cm^-1 are usable qualitative checks.
harvest_trust.ms: Untrusted axis calibration and no usable calibrated MS peak table supplied. Do not infer or emit experimental m/z values from this harvest.

patch_notes:
Scope: neutral, nonfused substituted benzene rings and simple acyclic saturated aliphatic environments, including the listed carbonyl derivatives. Values not supported by a stated harvest check are provisional chemistry priors, not experimentally fitted results. The pack cannot independently determine a full substituent library. Alkyl-substituent aromatic increments assume ordinary hydrocarbon side chains. Heteroaromatics, fused rings, charged species, alkenes, alkynes other than the listed nitrile functionality, aliphatic halides, multiply functionalized centers, and rigid stereochemical cases need separate rules or an unsupported/low-confidence flag.

_c_shift: identify each six-membered all-carbon aromatic ring and its exocyclic substituent attachments. Atom map :1 in every aromatic SMARTS identifies the ring ipso atom. Normalize ordinary nitro representations before matching. Classify each attachment once with the most specific applicable group; deduplicate SMARTS embeddings by ring, attachment atom, and substituent bond. Do not accumulate multiple matches for one substituent. For each ring carbon, start at 128.5 and add one increment per substituent according to distance along that ring: 0=ipso, 1=ortho, 2=meta, 3=para. A carbon bearing one substituent still receives ortho/meta/para effects from the other substituents. Never add one substituent once per atom in its SMARTS. Predict exocyclic carbonyl, nitrile, CF3, alkoxy, and alkyl carbons separately with absolute environment bins. Preserve unusual legitimate ring shifts such as aryl C-I near 94 ppm; do not clamp all aromatic carbons to 120–140 ppm.

_h_class: for each aromatic carbon actually bearing H, start at 7.27 and add the ortho/meta/para increment from every substituent on its ring, reusing the same attachment classifications as _c_shift. There is no ipso proton on a substituted site. Do not collapse all aromatic H into one class. Aldehyde H belongs to the exocyclic aldehyde carbon, not to the aromatic increment calculation. Aliphatic bins are absolute centers, not additive increments. Apply exact small-molecule and specific functional-group contexts before generic alkane, ether, amine, or alpha-carbonyl fallbacks. Distinguish ester O-CH2 from alcohol CH2OH and distinguish aromatic-ring attachment through O, N, or a carbonyl carbon. An atom matching multiple functional contexts needs an explicit combined rule or a low-confidence result rather than summed absolute bins.

Counts: determine chemical equivalence from the full molecular graph and relevant stereochemistry, not rounded shifts, local class labels, harvested stick counts, or intensity. Symmetry classes from RDKit CanonicalRankAtoms with breakTies=False can support carbon grouping; preserve chemically equivalent atoms rather than assigning each a unique canonical index. Assume an achiral solution and ordinary rapid methyl rotation. Proton counting additionally needs stereotopicity and exchange handling: graph ranks alone do not reliably distinguish diastereotopic CH2 hydrogens. Flag such cases if explicit stereotopicity logic is absent. Use equivalent-atom counts as carbon degeneracy and attached-proton totals as H integration, not as predicted peak height. Restricted amide rotation and slow conformational exchange are outside the simple count model.

Expected canary chemical-environment counts are benzaldehyde 13C=5 and nonexchangeable 1H=4; toluene 13C=5 and nonexchangeable 1H=4; nitrobenzene 13C=4 and nonexchangeable 1H=3; ethanol 13C=2 and nonexchangeable 1H=2 plus one potentially observable OH; acetic acid 13C=2 and nonexchangeable 1H=1 plus one potentially observable acid OH; ethyl acetate 13C=4 and 1H=3; 1-propanol 13C=3 and nonexchangeable 1H=3 plus one potentially observable OH; 2-propanol 13C=2 and nonexchangeable 1H=2 plus one potentially observable OH; acetone 13C=2 and 1H=1. Nitrobenzene therefore has three proton environments even though the harvest reports two envelopes. Keep environment count separate from optional display-envelope count. Approximate shift overlap may merge rendered envelopes but must not redefine equivalence. Do not use ±3 ppm or ±0.3 ppm prediction uncertainty as a peak-merging threshold.

Output resonance centers and integrations/degeneracies; multiplet simulation is a separate layer. In particular, C-F splitting, proton multiplet lines, and second-order aromatic patterns do not increase the number of chemical environments. Mark exchangeable signals as condition-dependent and potentially absent. Use broad uncertainty for generic aliphatic bins and additive polysubstituted predictions; do not promise the harvest tolerances for every table entry. Keep IR and MS behavior unchanged.
